faq.q: What is the significance of a date?
faq.a: A date becomes significant because of the meaning attached to it, usually an event that marked a before and after. People keep that meaning alive by remembering and marking the day.

faq.q: Why do some dates feel so emotional?
faq.a: Dates act as hooks for memory, so returning to one can bring back the feelings tied to what happened. Recurring dates also prompt us to compare where we are with where we were.

faq.q: How can I cope with a difficult anniversary?
faq.a: Put the date on your calendar so it doesn't surprise you, plan something gentle, and consider a small ritual. If grief feels overwhelming, reaching out to a friend or counselor can help.

faq.q: Can I create my own significant dates?
faq.a: Yes. Many people choose a personal new year, a sobriety anniversary, or a fresh-start date and give it meaning through ritual and reflection.

faq.q: What are some ways to celebrate meaningful dates?
faq.a: Simple rituals work well: revisiting a place, rereading letters, cooking a meaningful recipe, journaling, or sharing the story with someone you love.
